QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_33

question.text: Which of the following is NOT a valid reason to use a side-pocket arrangement in a Cat III open-ended AIF?

answer.text: An investee has become illiquid due to an idiosyncratic credit event
To protect existing investors from forced liquidation of a distressed asset
To enable new subscribers to enter at a clean NAV excluding the illiquid asset
To delay payment of management fees

explanation.text: The Logic: Side-pockets segregate illiquid/distressed assets from the main portfolio so NAV for main portfolio reflects only liquid assets. Management fees continue to accrue only on the LIQUID portfolio (side-pocket management-fee treatment varies per PPM). Side-pockets are NOT a fee-deferral mechanism. The Trap: A/B/C are legitimate reasons. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B Cat III Distributor covers side-pocket explanation to clients; XIX-E covers the operational/regulatory mechanics. Manager's Pro-Tip: On side-pocket creation, freeze subscriptions/redemptions for ~T+5, communicate a SEBI disclosure to all LPs within 24 hrs, and allocate side-pocket units pro-rata to LPs AT THE DATE OF SEGREGATION (not later).
